articles.title: Monday Night Football power outage caused by hilarious brain fart
articles.summary: Week 11 of the 2026 NFL regular season wrapped up on Monday Night Football with the Cincinnati Bengals visiting Northwest Stadium to take on the Washington Commanders under the lights… except for a few brief moments.
body: During the third quarter, there was a power outage at the stadium, and it went completely pitch black.
Some quick-thinking fans attempted to light up the venue with their cellphones, but that was obviously not enough. Joe Buck even got in a wise-crack about the entertaining sight.

Later in the broadcast, Buck revealed the actual reason for the power outage, and it was a reason so ridiculous you couldn’t make it up. As it turns out, they forgot that Monday Night Football was on Monday night.

“If you want to know the reason why the lights went out earlier, the official word is the lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 p.m.,” Buck said. “It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game.”

articles.title: Ella Swindle of Texas volleyball drafted by Indy Ignite in MLV draft, will turn pro
articles.summary: Texas volleyball senior setter Ella Swindle was selected 12th overall in the first round of the 2026 Major League Volleyball Draft by the Indy Ignite on Monday, becoming the third Longhorn selected in the league draft history. MLV will begin its fourth season in January.
body: Texas has had a player drafted in each of the last two years, with both selections made by the Indy Ignite. Former Texas libero Emma Halter got picked in the second round with the 14th overall pick of last year's MLV draft. Swindle and Halter were teammates at Texas for three seasons from 2023-25, including during the Longhorns' 2023 NCAA national championship season.
Swindle had one remaining year of eligibility but recently said she planned to leave Texas after four seasons.

"We are extremely excited for Ella and the opportunity to play for Indy Ignite," said Texas head coach Jerritt Elliott in a statement. "They are a first-class organization and will take great care of her. Having Ella reunite with Emma is a dream come true for both of them. I'm excited for Ella to reach her dreams, and we are confident in her ability to succeed."

Swindle joins middle blocker Asjia O'Neal and Halter as the three Texas players selected in league draft history. O'Neal was the first overall selection in the inaugural Pro Volleyball Federation Draft in 2023, becoming the first player ever selected in the league's draft. The league rebranded as Major League Volleyball ahead of the 2026 season.

articles.title: Cubs sign Trevor Rogers to multi-year deal
articles.summary: The Cubs have struck before the lockout hit to sign one of the top free agent pitchers: Big news tonight: Trevor Rogers and the Cubs have agreed on a multiyear deal. @MLBNetwork https://t.co/fzmea8dnq9. — Jon Morosi (@jonmorosi) November 24, 2026.
body: At this time we don’t have any terms for this deal, so that will have to wait till morning, most probably. But I wanted to make sure all of you had a place here to discuss this signing.
MLB Trade Rumors has him at five years, $115 million and The Athletic says four years, $84 million, basically the same AAV of $21 million.

Either one would be a good value, I believe. Over the last two seasons, Rogers has posted a 3.16 ERA and 1.074 WHIP in 48 starts covering 279.1 innings, with 260 strikeouts and only 68 walks. He’s also got a good home run rate, which given the Cubs staff’s issues with long balls this past season, is clearly a good thing.
MLB Trade Rumors, linked above, had Rogers as the No. 2 available starter this offseason, just behind Tarik Skubal.

articles.title: Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
articles.summary: Everton captain James Tarkowski was sent off for the first time in his Premier League career in Monday's 4-0 loss at Brentford - but was it a harsh decision?
body: Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record.
But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate.

His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history.
The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year.

articles.title: Five-time Solheim Cup player Khang secures LPGA Tour card for 2027
articles.summary: Megha Ganne won the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying stage as 27 tour cards were claimed for the 2027 season, with five-time USA Solheim Cup team member Megan Khang among those successful.
body: Khang - part of Team USA for the past five Solheim Cups - is returning to the LPGA Tour, on which she's made 259 starts since 2016, winning the 2023 CPKC Women's Open.
The top-25 finishers and ties at the conclusion of the 2026 LPGA Q-Series final qualifying were awarded LPGA Tour status for next year.

American Ganne won the final stage outright on 23 under, one shot clear of Shannon Tan and Julia Gregg in a tie for second. Min Sun7 Kim was fourth on 21 under and Xiaowen Yin one further back in fifth.
Ganne, the 2025 US Amateur champion, had actually already secured her 2027 LPGA Tour status by entering the week by finishing 11-15 on the Epson Tour.

articles.title: Patten ends Grand Slam-winning doubles pairing to partner fellow Brit Skupski
articles.summary: Henry Patten has ended his world No 1 doubles partnership with Harri Heliovaara in shock fashion in favour of teaming up with British compatriot Neal Skupski for 2027.
body: Patten and Heliovaara celebrated being crowned the best men's doubles team of the year at last week's ATP Finals after they claimed a second Wimbledon success together back in July.

However, in a post on Heliovaara's blog, the Finnish player revealed Patten phoned him on Friday to say their three-time Grand Slam-winning partnership was over - despite a previous agreement they would continue.

"After the trip to Turin, I didn't even have time to get into the holiday mood when the weekend took a rather unexpected turn," Heliovaara said on his own blog website. "Henry completely unexpectedly announced that he had changed his mind about next year.
"I picked up the kids from daycare on Friday afternoon and we were just opening presents when I got a call from Henry. Without going into too much detail, the message was clear.

articles.title: Penge claims stunning maiden PGA Tour win at RSM Classic
articles.summary: English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic.
body: Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.

With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.

Penge's five-under 65 on the Seaside Course included six birdies, including one at the last, and a single bogey, while he birdied 18 again to clinch victory in the playoff after nailing his approach to 10 feet.
"I always seem to play my best golf when my back's up against the wall," Penge said following his stunning win.

articles.title: The SEC Is Again Threatening To Kick Out LSU With A Vote Set For Next Week
articles.summary: A new court filing by the Southeastern Conference in a federal lawsuit against LSU states that conference plans to meet next week to vote on whether to expel LSU from the league it helped found.
body: The lawsuit, filed in Birmingham, Alabama, stems from LSU's recent attempts since the beginning of the fall semester to add football and basketball players who were recently under contract with NFL and NBA teams.

Although LSU and football coach Lane Kiffin decided against fielding two football players who'd won state court injunctions allowing them to play at the college level again, the Tigers' basketball team did play RJ Luis Jr. — who'd spent parts of the 2025 NBA offseason with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics — in a victory over Louisiana-Monroe last week.
"The lawsuit seeks to protect the Conference’s ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the SEC said in a statement Monday.

"The Conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs," the statement continued, adding that the new filing "advances the Conference’s obligation to defend its governance framework and the shared interests of its member universities."

articles.summary: The lights at Northwest Stadium went out during the third quarter of Monday night's game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes. The Commanders were in the red zone, trailing 10-7, when the stadium went dark and the game was halted.
body: It was later revealed that the lighting vendor forgot to cancel the regularly scheduled light maintenance at Northwest Stadium at 10 p.m., according to ESPN's broadcast of Monday night's game.
After a brief official timeout, the lights came back on and the game returned to action. Jayden Daniels threw an incomplete and the Commanders kicked a field goal to tie the game at 10-all.

articles.title: SEC schedules vote on possible LSU expulsion as RJ Luis dispute pushes league to the brink
articles.summary: LSU's standoff with the SEC has escalated into a legal and political fight, with major penalties still in play
body: The ongoing battle between the SEC and LSU took another significant turn Monday when the conference announced in a legal filing that it will hold a meeting in early December to consider expelling the school from the league.

The SEC's presidents and chancellors are scheduled to conduct a special meeting on Dec. 3, two days before the final SEC Championship Game in football, to "consider termination of LSU's membership to the SEC, regardless of whether LSU continues to play (RJ Luis)," per Monday's filing. It is the latest significant development in the standoff between LSU and the conference, which has included multiple lawsuits at both the state and federal levels over LSU trying to roster and play former professional players. It would take a two-thirds vote of qualifying members to purge LSU from the conference.
